name: Rubrik
thesis: Cyber-resilience platform displacing legacy backup/recovery vendors as enterprises consolidate ransomware recovery + cloud data protection onto a single subscription platform, then tack on adjacent modules (Identity, DSPM) to become multi-product. The bet: (1) subscription ARR keeps compounding above 25% YoY with growth endurance >=85% (deceleration is acceptable, a cliff is not), (2) NRR holds >120% as land-and-expand deepens, (3) multi-product attach widens the moat - customers >$1M ARR and Identity/DSPM ARR are the signals, (4) operating leverage inflects as the IPO-era CAC cycle normalizes. Not seat-exposed. Narrative kicker (NOT yet a tracked KPI): AI-agent proliferation drives a step-change in data/backup volumes. Competitive reality: Cohesity (post-Veritas) is now a scaled, profitable rival (~$1.5B ARR, targeting a 2026 IPO) - share gains must come against a funded peer, not just legacy incumbents.
key_driver: Net new subscription ARR cadence + sub ARR contribution margin inflection

nuance.bear_case: Cohesity (post-Veritas merger) is now a SCALED, profitable rival - it claims ~$1.5B ARR (larger than Rubrik's $1.46B), ~28% profit margin, deep Global-500 penetration, and is targeting a 2026 IPO. Backup/recovery is historically price-competitive once the differentiation cycle ends, and RBRK must take share against a funded peer that can out-spend on R&D and price-compete - not just legacy incumbents.
nuance.adversarial_take: 34% sub ARR growth at $1.5B base is excellent, but the law of large numbers will bend the trajectory by FY27. The thesis must accommodate growth deceleration to ~25% as the new normal without panicking — break threshold below 25% is calibrated for that.
nuance.stress_test: If $100K+ customer growth slows below 15% AND a competitor M&A creates a >$3B scaled rival, the moat thesis weakens even before any single break trips.
nuance.cohesity_competitive_update_2026_06: Post-Veritas, Cohesity is the bigger horse: ~$1.5B ARR, ~$1.7B revenue, ~28% profit margin, ~19% data-resilience share leader, NVIDIA-backed, targeting a 2026 IPO at ~$17B (~RBRK's cap). Positioning: Cohesity = 'the platform' (broad), RBRK = 'the specialist' (faster-growing, +32% sub-ARR Q1 FY27). The thesis is therefore 'the specialist out-grows the scaled incumbent' - RBRK must keep winning the INCREMENTAL net-new ARR even though Cohesity owns the larger installed base. The Cohesity IPO S-1 is the data-unlock for a direct share-of-net-new metric.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Subscription ARR growth endurance <85% (decelerating faster than thesis tolerates)
Net new sub ARR <$80M for 2 consecutive Qs
Sub ARR contribution margin reverses inflection
Major competitor M&A creating scaled rival (Cohesity-Veeam-Druva combination, etc.)

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion broken. (Universal floor; per-ticker FCF/SBC rules are stricter.)
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

business_model_rules.narrative: Subscription ARR YoY growth below 25% for 2 consecutive Qs — the law-of-large-numbers floor; below this the moat-attach thesis is in question.
Net new sub ARR < $80M for 2 consecutive Qs — deceleration to pre-FY26 cadence.
NRR < 115% — land-and-expand stalling within existing accounts.
Sub ARR contribution margin reverses below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — operating leverage thesis breaks (FY26 ran 11.6% vs 2.1% prior year).
Large-customer (>$100K ARR) count growing < 15% YoY — moat-attach signal weakening.
FCF margin below 10% for 2 consecutive Qs — FY26 ran ~13%, sub-10 is a structural cash-conversion regression (not the catastrophic 5% universal floor).
SBC as % of subscription revenue > 35% for 2 consecutive Qs — efficiency curve flatlining; the GAAP-margin-inflection thesis depends on this ratio falling.
